query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a secondary phase or precipitates through composition modification or processing could enhance the coercivity of single-phase fcc FeCoNi high-entropy alloys.
generation.intervention: Substitution of ferromagnetic Co with antiferromagnetic Cr or introduction of a secondary phase through processing
generation.conditions: Annealing at 600 °C for 15 h or other processing conditions that promote phase decomposition
generation.mechanism: Derived from materials-science principles, as the introduction of a secondary phase or precipitates can pin domain walls and enhance coercivity

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare single-phase fcc FeCoNi and FeCo0.5Cr0.5Ni alloys through arc melting and annealing, and measure their magnetic properties using VSM or SQUID
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coercivity of the FeCo0.5Cr0.5Ni alloy is not significantly higher than that of the single-phase fcc FeCoNi alloy, the hypothesis is falsified

Question: How does the substitution of ferromagnetic Co with antiferromagnetic Cr, combined with annealing temperature, influence the hierarchical phase decomposition, microhardness, and magnetic properties in AlCoFeNi-based high entropy alloys?. System: AlCoFeNi and AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi (near-equiatomic HEAs). Processing: Arc melting of elemental pellets (99.9% purity) under argon atmosphere, followed by isothermal annealing at 600 °C and 1000 °C for 15 h and water quenching. Test conditions: Annealing at 600 °C/15 h and 1000 °C/15 h; characterization via SEM, TEM, APT, EBSD, Vickers microhardness, and magnetic measurements (Ms, Hc). Findings: AlCoFeNi annealed at 1000 °C forms a single ordered B2 phase with a microhardness of 406 VHN, saturation magnetization (Ms) of 111.6 emu/g, and coercivity (Hc) of 4.3 Oe.; AlCoFeNi annealed at 600 °C decomposes into a B2 matrix and fine Fe-Co rich BCC precipitates, increasing microhardness to 474 VHN and Hc to 14.5 Oe while reducing Ms to 99.8 emu/g.; Substituting 50% Co with Cr in AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi induces phase separation into B2 + BCC even at 1000 °C, with Ms dropping to 42.2 emu/g and Hc rising to 39.4 Oe.; AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi anneal
